title: Total Factor Productivity's Contribution to GDP Growth in Past 10 Years
what_it_is: Total Factor Productivity's Contribution to GDP Growth in Past 10 Years

sections.label: Singapore Total Factor Productivity growth
sections.summary: Between 2008 and 2018 Singapore's TFP grew 0.5% yearly, rising to 0.9% since 2016, stronger than or comparable to most OECD countries.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Between 2008 and 2018, Singapore's Total Factor Productivity (TFP) grew by 0.5% per annum.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: This is about 12% of our gross domestic product (GDP) growth of 4.5% per annum over the same period.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Since 2016, TFP growth has increased to 0.9% per annum or around 27% of GDP growth.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Singapore's TFP performance was stronger than or comparable to most Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) countries.

sections.label: Economic restructuring raised productivity
sections.summary: The recent pickup in TFP growth is attributed to economic restructuring efforts to raise productivity and transform industries through innovation and internationalisation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The pickup in our TFP growth in recent years can be attributed to our economic restructuring efforts, which are important to raise productivity and to transform our industries through innovation and internationalisation.

sections.label: SkillsFuture and worker programmes
sections.summary: The Government says it understands Singaporeans' worries and has invested in SkillsFuture, Adapt and Grow and Professional Conversion Programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: To all fellow Singaporeans, I will say this: we understand your worries and we will walk this journey with you.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: This is why we have invested so much in SkillsFuture and programmes like Adapt and Grow and the Professional Conversion Programmes.

sections.label: Support for workers staying employable
sections.summary: The Government will do more to support Singaporeans who have not upgraded since starting work 20 years ago in staying skilled and employable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Many of them may not have done any upgrading since they started working 20 years ago after their studies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: And I want to assure this group of Singaporeans that the Government will do more to support them in staying skilled and employable, not just for now but also for the future.

sections.label: Foreign worker numbers trade-off
sections.summary: Too few foreign workers, especially PMETs, stop businesses seizing opportunities and creating better jobs, while too many cause push-back if Singaporeans feel unfairly treated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Too few foreign workers, especially PMETs with skills required for our growth sectors, mean that our businesses cannot seize the opportunities out there and, in the process, create better jobs for all Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Too many and there will be a push-back, especially if Singaporeans feel unfairly treated.

sections.label: Above average foreigners complement workforce
sections.summary: The passage states Singapore needs above average foreigners to complement the domestic workforce, building a more competitive economy with better jobs and pay for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Bring in the above average one to grow the economy, but below me." This summarises the fears, concerns and aspirations of our people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We know we need the above average foreigner to complement our domestic workforce so that we can build a more competitive economy and to provide better jobs and better pay for all Singaporeans.

sections.label: Early semiconductor companies create jobs
sections.summary: Three semiconductor companies created over 7,000 jobs in three years, but Singaporeans did not immediately get the best paying jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Over a span of three years, the first three semi-conductor companies in Singapore – National Semiconductor, Fairchild Semiconductor and Texas Instruments – created more than 7,000 jobs, but our people did not get the best paying jobs immediately.

sections.label: Skills gap for global investors
sections.summary: When Google, Grab and Facebook invest here, there are not enough Singaporeans with relevant skills and experience for all jobs created.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: When global companies like Google, Grab and Facebook invest here, the reality is that we do not have enough Singaporeans with the relevant skills and experience to fill all the jobs they are going to create.

sections.label: Risk of losing jobs
sections.summary: Otherwise the $7,000 job will be lost and the $10,000 job may never be obtained.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Otherwise, we will lose the $7,000 job and we may never get the $10,000 job.

sections.label: Fair Consideration Framework support
sections.summary: The Government understands concerns and stands with Singaporeans, so MOM has the Fair Consideration Framework and updates it for a fair playing field.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The Government understands these concerns, and we stand together with fellow Singaporeans on this matter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: This is why MOM has the Fair Consideration Framework (FCF) and is continually updating the system to ensure a fair, level playing field for Singaporeans.

sections.label: Action against unfair employers
sections.summary: If not, the Government will come down hard on them, has taken actions, and will not hesitate to do so again.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: If not, we will come down hard on them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We have taken actions against them, and we will not hesitate to do so again.

sections.label: Local employment and PMET share
sections.summary: Between 2015 and 2018, local employment rose by nearly 60,000 and the PMET share reached 57%, among the world's highest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Between 2015 and 2018, local employment increased by nearly 60,000 for the whole economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The PMET share of local employment increased to 57%, one of the highest rates in the world.

sections.label: Youth unemployment and education system
sections.summary: Youth unemployment is among the lowest in advanced economies, which the passage attributes to the education system providing the right foundation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Our youth unemployment is amongst the lowest amongst the advanced economies, a testimony to the fact that our education system is providing the right foundation for our people to take up those jobs that are being created in the new economy.

sections.label: Real average monthly earnings growth
sections.summary: Real average monthly earnings for employed local workers grew 3.2% per annum, higher than the preceding three years and than the US, Japan and Germany.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Growth in real average monthly earnings for employed local workers was 3.2% per annum during this period, higher than the 2.4% per annum in the preceding three years, higher than most advanced economies, such as the US, which is 0.5%; Japan, 0.8%; Germany, 1.2%.

sections.label: Calibrating balance of three factors
sections.summary: The Government will continue to calibrate a balance considering industries and enterprises, current workers, and opportunities for children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We have done the right things by getting that balance right and the Government will continue to calibrate this balance carefully.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: That balance is struck by considering three factors: the needs of our industries and enterprises, the needs of our workers of this generation and the opportunities for our children in the next generation.

sections.label: Pass criteria and workforce ratios
sections.summary: S Pass and Employment Pass criteria were raised, Services DRC and S Pass sub-DRC reduced, and PMET share and citizen unemployment figures given.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: For example, we raised the S Pass minimum qualifying criteria in 2019 and 2020 as well as the Employment Pass minimum qualifying criteria in 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: This helps us keep pace with rising local wages and enhance the foreign workforce complementarity to the local workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: We are also reducing the Services sector dependency ratio ceiling (DRC) and S Pass sub-DRC over 2020 and 2021 to push businesses to become more manpower-lean and improve job quality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: The PMET share of local employment rose from 54% in 2015 to 57% in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Citizen unemployment is 3% in 2018 and has averaged 3.1% since 2015.

sections.label: Updating FCF and stiffer penalties
sections.summary: The Minister for Manpower announced plans to update the FCF, with stiffer penalties for businesses that deliberately exclude qualified Singaporean jobseekers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Just last week, the Minister for Manpower announced plans to update the FCF, and businesses that deliberately exclude qualified Singaporean jobseekers will suffer stiffer penalties.

sections.label: Considering investments for Singaporean jobs
sections.summary: For each investment, the passage says land, carbon and energy constraints are considered and whether it will create a good job for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: People have asked me, "Why do we not go and take all the investments that are queuing up at our doors?" And that is a simple way to do so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: But for every investment that we take into Singapore today, we not only consider the land constraints, the carbon constraints, the energy usage and all that kind of things but, most importantly, as the Member has said, we ask ourselves is this going to create a good job for Singaporeans?

sections.label: Cost and quality control
sections.summary: Each one costs $20,000 to $30,000 and has high-quality control.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Each one is $20,000 to $30,000, with high-quality control.

sections.label: TFP after Global Financial Crisis
sections.summary: In the year of rebounding from the Global Financial Crisis, TFP was over 9%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: In fact, as an example, during the Global Financial Crisis, when we rebounded from the Global Financial Crisis, that particular year, our TFP was over 9%.

sections.label: Three sectors holding up economy
sections.summary: Banking and Finance, Professional Services and ICT are three sectors holding up the economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: On the other hand, there are three sectors, three shining examples holding up the economy – Banking and Finance, Professional Services, ICT.

sections.label: Skills top-up for older workers
sections.summary: More plans to tackle this challenge will be announced in the Budget, as people in their 40s and 50s need a skills top-up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: This is a challenge which the whole world is waking up to, but not the whole world has the means and the organisation to tackle this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We will announce more plans to tackle this in the Budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We know that people in their 40s and 50s, including those in the ICT sector, they need a skills top-up, they need a refresh.

sections.label: Top up workers' skills
sections.summary: Every 10 years or so, if affordable and organised, the skills of every worker should be topped up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The correct approach is that every 10 years or so, if we can afford it and have the organisation, we should top up the skills of each and every one of our workers.

sections.label: Continuous training and lifelong employability
sections.summary: Continuous training must be in our DNA to get lifelong employability and not lifelong employment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Continuous training must be in our DNA and then we can get into lifelong employability and not lifelong employment.

sections.label: Growing jobs for underemployed
sections.summary: MTI is strengthening mid-sized companies to create more and better-paying jobs for underemployed Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: What is most important to get people out of underemployment is to grow the job opportunities for them to go on and take on better-paying jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: This is why, in MTI's strategy, we are spending so much effort to strengthen the mid-sized companies, so that they can create more and better-paying jobs, more opportunities, for the rest of Singaporeans who are not in such high-paying jobs to get into those jobs.

sections.label: Local PMET share rise
sections.summary: The Minister for Trade and Industry said the local PMET share rose from 54% to 57%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: The Minister for Trade and Industry spoke of the local PMET share going up from 54% to 57%.

sections.label: Data requests and speed
sections.summary: The speaker says asking for data is pointless if Government will not provide it, and that it is faster than many countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: Because it is pointless for us to keep asking for the data if the Government is not going to provide it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We can get the Member the numbers but let me say this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Yes, and it is faster than many other countries.

sections.label: Jobs going to Singaporeans
sections.summary: Enough of the increased jobs go to Singaporeans to keep unemployment at a level many countries would call fiction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: How many of the increased jobs go to Singaporeans?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Enough for us to keep the unemployment rate at the level which many countries would say it is fiction.
